title: Age of Discovery
summary: European navigators cross unknown oceans and redraw the map of the world — from Columbus's first Atlantic crossing to the routes that linked continents by sea.

stories.title: Columbus & the New World
stories.summary: The 1492 voyage that opened sustained European contact with the Americas.

events.title: Departure from Palos
events.body: Three ships — the Niña, Pinta, and Santa María — left Palos de la Frontera under the Castilian crown. Columbus sailed west, betting that Asia lay across the Atlantic.

events.title: Canary Islands
events.body: The fleet stopped at La Gomera in the Canaries to take on supplies and make final repairs. From there Columbus turned west into the open Atlantic on the longest leg of the voyage.

events.title: Landfall at Guanahani
events.body: After thirty-three days at sea, land was sighted in the Bahamas. Columbus went ashore on an island the Taíno called Guanahani, believing he had reached the Indies.

events.title: Hispaniola
events.body: Exploring farther, Columbus reached Hispaniola and founded La Navidad — the first European settlement in the New World. The Santa María ran aground and her timbers were used to build the fort.

events.title: Return to Spain
events.body: Columbus sailed home with gold, captive Taíno people, and news of new lands. His return to Palos set off a wave of exploration that would reshape trade, empire, and the map itself.

stories.title: Da Gama to India
stories.summary: Portugal opens a sea route to India around the Cape of Good Hope.

stories.title: Magellan's Circumnavigation
stories.summary: The first voyage to circle the globe, completed by Elcano.
